Our proposed revisions require diligence and the headline price to be settled before signing, limit adjustments to an agreed completion-accounts mechanism, and retain the 30-day closing timetable. We propose a 10% escrow for 12 months, a deductible basket and proportionate liability caps, with distinct treatment for fundamental warranties, taxes and actual fraud. Timely notified claims would survive pending resolution. Please confirm whether these terms provide a basis for finalizing the agreement and schedules.

edits.text: PARTIES. This Agreement is between each person identified as a seller in Schedule 1 (each a Seller and together the Sellers) and Meridian Acquisitions LLC as Buyer. Schedule 1 shall identify all registered and beneficial owners, their respective holdings and consideration allocations. All such owners shall execute this Agreement or binding transfer documentation sufficient to convey their interests. Each Seller's obligations and liability shall be several, not joint.

1. PURCHASE AND PURCHASE PRICE. At Closing, the Sellers shall transfer to Buyer 100% of the issued and outstanding Shares, free of liens, with all options, warrants and other rights to acquire Shares exercised, cancelled or otherwise discharged under arrangements agreed before signing. The parties shall agree and insert a fixed headline Purchase Price before signing. The Purchase Price shall be adjusted solely for cash, debt and normalized working capital under definitions, a working-capital target and an illustrative calculation agreed and attached before signing, without double counting. Buyer shall deliver completion accounts within 60 days after Closing; Sellers shall have 30 days to object, and unresolved accounting disputes shall be determined by an independent accountant acting as expert. Buyer shall have no unilateral right to reprice the transaction based on diligence. At Closing, Buyer shall pay 90% of the estimated adjusted Purchase Price to Sellers and deposit 10% with an independent escrow agent. The escrow shall be released 12 months after Closing, less only reasonable amounts reserved for specifically identified, timely notified unresolved claims; reserved amounts shall be released promptly upon resolution.

2. CLOSING. Closing shall occur as soon as the conditions are satisfied and no later than 30 days after signing, unless extended by written agreement. Buyer shall complete its diligence before signing; neither further diligence nor financing shall be a Closing condition. Closing conditions shall be limited to receipt of the required third-party and regulatory consents specifically listed at signing, delivery of executed transfers and agreed lien releases, absence of any legal prohibition, and delivery of a certificate confirming that Seller warranties remain true in all material respects at Closing, except that warranties already qualified by materiality shall be tested as written. Buyer shall deliver the Closing consideration and evidence of its authority. Each party shall use reasonable best efforts to satisfy the conditions and may not rely on a condition's failure caused by its own breach. If Closing has not occurred by the deadline, either non-defaulting party may terminate by notice, without prejudice to accrued rights.

3. REPRESENTATIONS. Each Seller warrants its title to its Shares, capacity and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement. Sellers further warrant the Company's capitalization; that its accounts fairly present its financial position in all material respects under the accounting principles identified in the accounts; material tax compliance; compliance with applicable laws in all material respects; the validity of material contracts and absence of material defaults; absence of pending or, to Sellers' knowledge, threatened material litigation; and absence of material liabilities required to be reflected in those accounts other than liabilities disclosed or incurred in the ordinary course since their date. These warranties are subject to specific, fair disclosure in the disclosure schedules agreed at signing. Sellers' knowledge means the actual knowledge of designated individuals following reasonable inquiry of responsible personnel. Buyer warrants its authority and availability at Closing of sufficient immediately available funds. No Seller gives a warranty as to projections or future performance.

4. INDEMNITY. Subject to this clause, Sellers shall indemnify Buyer for actual losses resulting from breaches of the express warranties or covenants, pre-Closing taxes and liabilities existing at Closing that were neither fairly disclosed nor reflected in the final Purchase Price calculation. Ordinary warranty and undisclosed-liability claims shall survive for 12 months after Closing, be subject to a deductible basket equal to 1% of the final Purchase Price, and have an aggregate cap equal to 10% of that price; escrow shall be the exclusive source of recovery for those claims. Title, authority and capitalization claims shall survive for six years; pre-Closing tax claims shall survive until 60 days after expiry of the applicable statutory assessment period. Those claims and covenant claims shall not be subject to the basket or escrow exclusivity, but total liability for all claims against any Seller shall not exceed the consideration received by that Seller. Covenant claims shall survive for 12 months after the applicable performance period ends. No limitation shall protect a Seller against its own actual fraud, and no Seller shall be liable for another person's fraud. Buyer shall give reasonably detailed written notice of a claim within its applicable survival period; a timely notified claim shall survive solely as to the matters identified until finally resolved. For third-party claims, Sellers may assume the defense with competent counsel, except where a material conflict or nonmonetary relief affecting Buyer makes that inappropriate; no settlement imposing an admission, nonmonetary obligation or unreimbursed payment on Buyer may be entered without Buyer's reasonable consent. Buyer shall mitigate losses, and recovery shall exclude duplicate recoveries, amounts accounted for in the Purchase Price, and amounts actually recovered from insurance or third parties, net of reasonable recovery costs. Punitive damages shall be excluded except where payable to a third party. Except for actual fraud and equitable enforcement of express obligations, this clause provides the exclusive monetary remedies for matters covered by it.

receiver.message_back: The agreed pre-signing price and diligence process, completion-accounts mechanism and 30-day closing timetable provide a basis to finalize, subject to satisfactory schedules and these remaining protections: an 18-month ordinary-claim period and 10% escrow, a 0.5% deductible basket, and a 20% ordinary-claim cap with direct recourse above escrow. Pre-Closing taxes and undisclosed Closing liabilities must remain separately recoverable without the ordinary-claim basket or escrow exclusivity, subject to each Seller’s consideration cap, with timely notified claims preserved until resolution and the actual-fraud carve-out retained.
